characters.name: Burrowing Parakeet
characters.description: A colorful species of parrot native to Patagonia in South America. It is named for its habit of digging out burrows in limestone or sandstone cliff faces.

characters.name: South American Short-Faced Bear
characters.description: A South American species of tremarctine bear larger than any other bear to have lived. Like many other predatory South American mammals existing during the Ice Age, its ancestors originated from North America. Bears Are Bad News: Zig-zagged, withBeary Friendly. Like extant bears, he's mostly placid and is first introduced resting in a clearing... but the narrator notes thathe is a powerful predatorand is unafraid to use his immense size and strength when he needs to (such as when he needs to bully smaller predators off their kill). The Bully: Like all large ursids, he prefers to use his sheer size to bully smaller carnivores of their kill - in this case, a pack of South American wild dogs.Although, unlike most examples, he's only doing it because it's an easy meal. Dire Beast: A cousin of the modestly sized spectacled bear growing bigger than even a polar bear. Super-Strength: As to be expected from a bear of its size. It breaks aProtocyon's leg with a light swat.

characters.name: Protocyon
characters.description: A mid-sized, pack-hunting canid belonging to a uniquely South American lineage of dogs known as the cerdocyonines. David vs. Goliath: The pack tries to drive away the humongousArctotheriumfrom their kill. Of course, it doesn't work, and one dog receives an injured leg for its troubles. Dire Beast: Looks like a larger, more cursorial version of the short-eared dog. End of an Age: Their scuffle with the short-faced bear symbolizes this. Cerdocyonins were the first hypercarnivores to colonize South America at the beginning of the Great American Interchange (circa 2.5 mya), facing little competition aside from the dog-like raccoon relativeCyonasuanoteProcyonids were the first carnivorans to colonize South America, around 7.3 million years ago.and (supposedly) 3-foot-high psilopterine terror birdsnoteThe age of the Late Pleistocene fossils from Uruguay is controversial., withProtocyonspecifically adapting for hunting large game, akin to dholes. However, they were outclassed once the largerArctotheriumand saber-toothed cat arrived in South America around a million years later, followed by the dire wolf, cougar and jaguar as well, ensuring thatProtocyonwas far from an apex predator anymore. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: Of dholes, another unassuming-looking canid known to take on very large game and boldly face off against much larger predators like tigers. Though as a cerdocyonin, it is more closely related to zorros, bush dogs, short-eared dogs and the bizarre maned wolf.

characters.name: Giant Ground Sloth
characters.description: A megatheriid ground sloth from the rainforests of Central and South America the size of an elephant. Owing to it sheer bulk, this strange-looking giant is mostly hairless, although just like its shaggier kin, it is a docile vegetarian. Big Guy, Little Guy: With the variegated squirrel, which follows the giant sloth around in order to scavenge whatever fruit the sloth drops while eating. Dub Name Change: Being called a "giant ground sloth" led toEremotheriumin the German dub being referred to by the name of the most famous giant ground sloth, its close relativeMegatherium. Mighty Glacier: It's a sloth but the size of an elephant and armed withWolverine Claws, leaving adults safe from predators like sabretooths and dire wolves. No Name Given: The species is not identified in the show, but has been confirmed in the press release, supported by its presence in a Central/northern South American rainforest habitat, as opposed to the more southernly range of the better-known, similarly sizeMegatherium.

characters.name: Glyptotherium
characters.description: A glyptodont armadillo that inhabits the scrublands of the southern United States and Mexico. Its ancestors evolved in South America, but following the formation of the Isthmus of Panama, they have migrated north, making the only species of glyptodont found in North America. No Name Given: It is only referred to in the show as a "giant armadillo", but its species was confirmed in early press releases. Plus, there is only one glyptodont species that ever overlapped with Columbian mammoths.

characters.name: Columbian Mammoth
characters.description: A larger, less hairy relative of the woolly mammoth native to the temperate and subtropical climates of North and Central America. Appears in "New Lands" and "The Big Melt". Cruel Elephant: Downplayed. One bad-tempered bull drives off aGlyptotheriumand her young from a watering hole. Decoy Protagonist: Just like theAlamosaurusfrom season 2, a Columbian mammoth is initially portrayed as the main character of a segment where it dies at the start to make way for a confrontation of two carnivores over its carcass. Hair-Trigger Temper: As mentioned above, a huge male gets triggered at the sight of the "Glyptotherium" and her baby, and aggressively scares them away. Plot-Triggering Death: It getting stuck in the tar pits triggers a squabble between a sabertooth mother and a pack of dire wolves for the carcass.

characters.name: Sumba DwarfStegodon
characters.description: A three-foot-tall species of proboscidean found on the island of Sumba in Indonesia. It is not especially closely related to mammoths or modern elephants, instead representing a now-extinct family that was widespread across Asia during the Ice Age. Fun Size: Compared to their mainland counterparts and modern elephants, these pint-sized proboscideans are outright adorable. Honorable Elephant: TheStegodonfamily shows to have a close bond with each other. Mama Bear: The motherStegodonfends off three giant storks that were trying to eat her baby. No Name Given: Subverted. Identified in the show as a species ofStegodon— most viewers assumed it was the dwarf species from Flores,S. florensis, but Darren Naish confirmed it as the even smaller speciesS. sumbaensisin a Reddit thread.

characters.name: Flores Giant Stork
characters.description: A man-sized species of stork from the island of Flores in Indonesia closely related to the marabou stork of Africa and the adjutant storks of Asia. They are among the chief predators of their island home, hunting any creature small enough for them to spear with their beaks. Beak Attack: Like their modern cousins, they use their beaks as deadly weapons and hunting tools. Dire Beast: It's a marabou/adjutant stork as tall as a grown man. Granted, extant species aren't far behind. Feathered Fiend: This is a stork as tall as a man, and it is a dangerous predator and scavenger with a sharp beak that preys onelephants(dwarf elephants, but still). Misplaced Wildlife: Despite its fossils being found on the island of Flores, it is shown hunting the dwarfStegodonon Sumba.Justified, as the show identifies it as an island-hopper.

characters.name: Psilopterus
characters.description: A small, predatory, flightless bird found in South America related to the modern seriemas that still roam the continent today. It is the last of the phorusrhacids (or "terror birds"), a uniquely South American group had previously produced numerous large apex predators that hunted the native plant-eating mammals. Anachronistic Animal: A controversial example. Fragmentary fossils of aPsilopterus-like form from Uruguay (the type species ofPsilopterusoriginates from strata dating to 18-15 mya) have been interpreted as dating to the Late Pleistocene, though the dating methods used have been brought into question. That said, in March 2026, remains assigned to aPsilopterus-sized terror bird namedEschatornis("last bird") were discovered in Brazil, confirming that small terror birds made it to the Late Pleistocene after all. Deathbringer the Adorable: They are only referred to as "terror birds" in the documentary. While taxonomically accurate, the name is much more befitting of their larger and older relatives. It's even lampshaded.The local competition: a terror bird. Maybe not that terrifying, but intelligent, resourceful, flightless hunters. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: To caracaras, with a bit of seriema thrown in. Fun Size: It's only 3 feet tall compared to the very largest phorusrhacids likeKelenkenandDevincenzia, which stood 7-8 feet tall. It's essentially a slightly more robust seriema. Of course, phorusrhacids were a diverse family that came in all sorts of sizes.

characters.name: Variegated Squirrel
characters.description: A distinctly colored species of squirrel found in the rainforests of Central America. During the Ice Age, small rodents like them would have followed large herbivores, like giant ground sloths, to feed on plant material left behind in the bigger animals' feedings. Big Guy, Little Guy: The little to the giant ground sloth's big, which it follows to get fruit the giant sloth drops from the treetops.

characters.name: Spectacled Bear
characters.description: A smaller species of tremarctine bear found in the northern parts of South America. It is very closely related to the giant short-faced bears that also roamed the Americas during the Ice Age.

characters.name: Yellow-throated Toucan
characters.description: A species of toucan native to Central and South America.

characters.name: White-booted Racket-tail
characters.description: A hummingbird found in northern South America.

characters.name: Tailorbird
characters.description: A type of passerine native to Asia. They are named for their behavior of "sewing" leaves together using plant fiber and spiderwebs to build nests.

characters.name: Ulysses Butterfly
characters.description: A species of swallowtail butterfly found in the rainforests of Southeast Asia, Australia, New Guinea, and the Solomon Islands. Appears in "New Lands" and "Grass Lands".

characters.name: Diabolotherium
characters.description: A small species of megatheriid ground sloth native to the Andes Mountains of South America. Like modern sloths, it is an adept climber, but instead of an arboreal lifestyle, it specializes in scaling mountain cliffsides. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: It is the giant sloth equivalent of a mountain climbing goat, such as an ibex. Mama Bear: The mother sloth fights off teratorns to protect her baby, even chasing them out of her den. No Name Given: The show only dubs them "rock sloths". This infamously caused quite a bit of confusion for viewers, with fans debating about whether it is the North AmericanNothrotheriops(the Shasta ground sloth) or the more obscure, South AmericanDiabolotherium, until it was confirmed by Darren Naish that it was in fact the latter. The narration certainly doesn't help by not even explaining that the rock sloth and teratorn segment takes place in Peru. Ridiculously Cute Critter: The baby sloth is just adorable!

characters.name: Teratorn
characters.description: A large raptor related to condors and New World vultures, being likewise found across the Americas. Unlike their scavenging cousins, these huge birds are active predators. Brutal Bird of Prey: They are depicted harassing aDiabolotheriumfamily to make them fall to their deaths. Downplayed since they are just animals looking for their next meal. Dire Beast: Giant vulture relatives that hunt on the clifftops. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: Being a bird of prey that's attacking mammals on rocky mountain cliffs, it is no surprise that this behavior is lifted from golden eagles. Its colors and proclivity towards hunting land-bound prey also makes it resemble a crested caracara. Feathered Fiend: It harasses theDiabolotheriummother and cub.

characters.name: Diprotodon
characters.description: A rhinoceros-sized, herd-living marsupial related to wombats. They are the largest terrestrial herbivores in Pleistocene Australia, trekking endlessly across the increasingly arid Outback on an endless search for food and water. Dire Beast: It was basically a rhino-sized wombat. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: Of elephants and camels, as they live in matriarchal herds, led by the eldest female who memorizes the long paths between waterholes, and also cross vast deserts in search for water while settling disputes in a more aggressive fashion, using their powerful jaws. Hope Spot: Zigzagged. While it seems at first the new leader has led the herd to a dry area dooming them to die of dehydration, she ends up digging up groundwater from a river bed. Although the new leader manages to find water, the narrator notes how with Australia's climate getting drier and deserts more ubiquitous across the continent, things will only get worse for theDiprotodon.

characters.name: Marsupial Lion
characters.description: A carnivorous marsupial related to wombats and koalas that convergently evolved to fill the niche of big cats in the Australian outback, becoming one of the apex carnivores of the Land Down Under and perhaps the strangest carnivore of the Ice Age. Artistic License – Paleontology: Marsupial lions could likely run much faster than 10 mph, at least for short distances. Using one of their closest extant relatives for reference, wombats can reach top speeds of 25 mph in short bursts, and they are evenlesscursorial than the marsupial lion was. Ascended to Carnivorism: A cousin of wombats and koalas that became an obligate carnivore. Its bizarre stabbing incisors are modified from its herbivorous ancestors. Crippling Overspecialization: They're adapted for ambushing and wrestling prey at close quarters — their running speed is less than 10 mph. As a result, they're shown struggling to catch prey in the largely bare desert habitat. Death from Above: Pouncing from trees works better for them than pursuit on foot.

characters.name: Procoptodon
characters.description: A giant sthenurine kangaroo and the largest kangaroo to have ever existed. Due to its immense size, it walked instead of hopping like all its living relatives do. Death of a Child: A baby is ambushed and killed by the female marsupial lion that was hiding in the tree above it. Mighty Glacier:P. goliahis the largest known kangaroo species of all time. So large, in fact, that it's unable to hop like its extant relatives, and its top running speed is a rather unimpressive 10 mph. Fortunately for it, many of its potential predators (which include the likes ofThylacoleoand Megalania) are even slower. Shown Their Work: Unlike depictions from the 2000s, they are accurately shown as being incapable of hopping, only walking on two legs. Stock Animal Behavior: Averted. These kangaroos don't jump— theywalk, in a rather bizarre fashion.

characters.name: North Island Giant Moa
characters.description: A giant ratite bird native to New Zealand. Taking on the ecological role held in the rest of the world by giant mammals, the females of their kind are the tallest birds to have ever lived. Males on the other hand are less than half the size of the females. They also disappeared much more recently than most of the other extinct animals featured in this show, vanishing sometime during the Middle Ages. Armless Biped: They lack even vestigial wings. Bizarre Sexual Dimorphism: Males are much smaller, but more brightly coloured than the females. Has a Type: Female giant moa prefer males who are very small, since they can incubate the eggs more easily. Masculine Girl, Feminine Boy: The female is larger, more short-tempered and physically stronger than her mate, who takes on the traditionally feminine nurturing parent role due to the female being too large to safely incubate their egg.

characters.name: Propleopus
characters.description: An unusual marsupial closely related to the musky rat-kangaroo, the small living kangaroo species. Although much larger than its modern relative, it shares the omnivorous diet, in contrast to the rest of their more traditionally herbivorous kin. Ascended to Carnivorism: A macropod species that became a bear-like omnivore. Dire Beast: A downplayed example. Compared to its closest living relative, the 500-gram, 10-inch long musky rat-kangaroo,Propleopusappears enormous. But at a little under a meter tall and up to 70 kilos in weight, it's thoroughly dwarfed by mega-marsupial behemoths likeDiprotodonandProcoptodon. Mix-and-Match Critter: It resembles a cross between a mongoose and a wallaby. No Name Given: They're only identified as being a kind of kangaroo, but their appearance and taste for small animals gives away their identity.

characters.name: Megalania
characters.description: A giant monitor lizard from Australia closely related to the living Komodo dragon. It was the largest lizard alive during the Ice Age and one of the top predators of its continent. Artifact Name: The species was originally described in its own genus as, "Megalania prisca", separate from modern monitor lizards (Varanus), but it is now known that it was a true monitor lizard, specifically related to Komodo dragons. Dire Beast: Basically a Komodo dragon (which were also native to Australia during the Pleistocene) but scaled up to the size of a large crocodilian. Eats Babies: Has zero qualms about gobbling up a baby of its own kind, and it also tries to eat the babyPropleopus. Malicious Monitor Lizard: There is no malice in its actions, only the instinct to feed itself, but trying to eat cute little baby roos and even cannibalising conspecific babies certainly evokes this trope.

characters.name: Thorny Devil
characters.description: A spiny, insectivorous agama lizard native to the deserts of Australia. Its spines are used for defense, but also assist it in collecting water.

characters.name: Bearded Dragon
characters.description: An agama lizard from the Australian Outback.

characters.name: Wedge-tailed Eagle
characters.description: A large eagle native to Australia. These formidable birds of prey typically hunt live prey, but they also freely take advantage of carrion. Circling Vultures: They are capable of hunting and killing their own prey, but they also feed on carrion (likeDiprotodoncarcasses) in a similar manner to vultures.

characters.name: New Zealand Dung Beetle
characters.description: A coprophagous insect that rolls up balls of poop to present to potential mates. Whereas dung beetles elsewhere in the world feed on mammal dung, the dung beetles of New Zealand mainly eat moa poop.

characters.name: New Zealand Bellbird
characters.description: A species of honeyeater native to New Zealand.

characters.name: Rainbow Bee-eater
characters.description: The only species of bee-eater known from Australia.

characters.name: Crested Pigeon
characters.description: A species of Australian pigeon with a tall crest.

characters.name: Galah
characters.description: A species of cockatoo native to Australia with a distinctive pink and grey coloration.

characters.name: Flinders Range Scorpion
characters.description: A species of scorpion endemic to Australia and one of the continent's largest scorpions.

characters.name: Elasmotherium
characters.description: A hairy, elephant-sized rhinoceros found across the mammoth steppes of Eurasia. Contrasting with the massive nasal horns of its fellow Ice Age rhinos, it instead has a single large boss on top of its head. Dire Beast: It's a boreal rhinoceros like the woolly rhino but comparable in size to an Asian elephant and only marginally smaller than a woolly mammoth. No Name Given: Only called a "rhinoceros" by the show, but its species was confirmed in press releases. Rhino Rampage: Averted. BothElasmotheriumhave a peaceful encounter and enjoy a mud bath together. Shown Their Work: Rather than sporting a 2-meter horn like traditional depictions (alaPrehistoric Park), it has smaller boss based on more recent studies (though this idea has popped up in older paleo-art from time to time too).

characters.name: African Scimitar Cat
characters.description: A species ofHomotheriumfound in sub-Saharan Africa. While its Eurasian and North American relatives inhabited the icy landscapes of the far north, this one roams the great savannahs of Africa. Artistic License – Biology: Likely due tosharing the same modelas the two boreal scimitar cats, its fur looks too thick and shaggy for a big cat living on the sweltering plains of Africa. Even weirder, since the Patagonian saber-toothed cat (Smilodon populator) and Californian saber-toothed cat (Smilodon fatalis) also share the same model, yet the latter has more short-cropped fur to go along with the warmer environment it lives in. Anachronistic Animal: LikeEnhydriodon, the last of Africa's scimitar cats vanished in the Early Pleistocene (at least 1.5 mya), when all the other fauna in the series survived until the end or close to the end of the Pleistocene (some well into the Holocene). Cool vs. Awesome: It fights the giant otter. Palette Swap: Shares the same model as the Eurasian and North American scimitar cat. Justified, as they are congeneric species and morphologically very homogenous.

characters.name: Oldoway Zebra
characters.description: An extinct species of zebra related to Grevy's zebra (and possibly ancestral to it), likewise inhabiting the plains of Africa. Anachronistic Animal: Similar toEnhydriodonand the AfricanHomotherium, this zebra species disappeared in the Early Pleistocene, with no indication as to whether the segment is set further back in time compared to the other segments. At least in this case, zebras as a wholewould have inhabited Africa throughout the Pleistocene, since they're still around. Monster Munch: It only serves as a prey animal for theHomotherium. No Name Given: This zebra's species is not confirmed in the episode, and was only confirmed by Darren Naish after the show aired. He even specifically pointed out that, if looking closely, the zebra had anatomical traits which could help distinguish it from the extant Grevy's zebra. Plot-Triggering Death: Its carcass becomes a fierce battleground between the scimitar cats and theEnhydriodon.

characters.name: Enhydriodon
characters.description: A lion-sized species of otter that roamed the African plains and was closely related to the living sea otter. While just as sociable as its relatives, its larger size and more terrestrial lifestyle means it preferred much more substantial prey than seafood. Anachronistic Animal: Like the African scimitar cat, the last ofEnhydriodonvanished in the very early Pleistocene, and the segment makes no indication that it's set further back in time than the others. Dire Beast: It was an otter the size of a lion. It and a few congeneric species are in fact the largest known mustelids. The Family That Slays Together: Like Amazonian giant otters, they live in tightly knit family units, including the little babies. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: Of Amazonian giant otters,only even more giant. They likewise travel in groups and aren't scared of confronting big cats (like giant otters with jaguars), except here, they are big enough to take on the big cat one-on-one.

characters.name: Gigantopithecus
characters.description: A giant ape related to the orangutan found in the bamboo forests of southern China. Although the largest primate to have ever lived, these marvelous creatures have been in decline as the tumultuous climate change of the Ice Age reduces their preferred habitat. Ascended to Carnivorism: Downplayed. Like gorillas, they are shown to be primarily herbivorous, but fond of eating insects if the opportunity presents itself. The male is shown feeding on ants that it catches with a stick similar to chimpanzees. Bigfoot, Sasquatch, and Yeti: Parodied when it's walking on its hind legs in a forest (albeit with the help of a large stick), reminiscent of classic bigfoot depictions. Quite fittingly, bigfeet and yetis are often believed to be survivingGigantopithecus. Dire Beast: A giant orangutan relative with the build of a gorilla, and larger than both. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: Basically Asia's version of the gorilla, a giant, herbivorous, forest-dwelling ape.

characters.name: Doedicurus
characters.description: A glyptodont armadillo native to the drier landscapes of Patagonia in South America. It is distinguished by the spiky club at the end of its tail, which males use to bash each other in mating disputes. Beware My Stinger Tail: Their clubbed tail is their primary defensive weapon. Compete for the Maiden's Hand: An older and younger male try courting the same female and start clubbing each other in a show of strength. The younger male wins. Dented Iron: The older male's armor is scarred from earlier fights. Did Not Get the Girl: Despite his victory, the female rejects the young male's advances.

characters.name: Kori Bustard
characters.description: A species of bustard and the largest flying bird in Africa, being among the largest flying birds to survive to the modern day.

characters.name: Northern Carmine Bee-eater
characters.description: A species of bee-eater native to Africa. It can be distinguished from its sister species the southern carmine bee-eater (which it was once deemed the same species as) by its blue throat.

characters.name: Southern Carmine Bee-eater
characters.description: A species of bee-eater native to Africa. It can be distinguished from its sister species the northern carmine bee-eater (which it was once deemed the same species as) by its pink throat.

characters.name: Bison
characters.description: Large bovines found in cooler climes of the Northern Hemisphere. During the Ice Age, many species, both living and extinct, ranged across the prairies of North America and the mammoth steppes of Eurasia.

characters.name: Ticks
characters.description: Parasitic arachnids that drink the blood of large mammals. Even Ice Age giants must regularly rid themselves of these bothersome pests.

characters.name: Common Raven
characters.description: A large and widespread species of corvid. These clever birds pluck tufts of fur from the bodies of megafaunal mammals to use as insulation for their nests. Appears in "Grass Lands" and "The Big Melt".

characters.name: Common Ostrich
characters.description: A large ratite native to Africa, and the largest bird to survive to modern times.

characters.name: Black Giant Squirrel
characters.description: A cat-sized species of tree squirrel found in Southeast Asia.

characters.name: Rhesus Macaque
characters.description: A species of Old World monkey widespread across the Indian subcontinent, southern China, and southeast Asia

characters.name: Dusky Leaf Monkey
characters.description: A species of Old World monkey found in Southeast Asia.

characters.name: Lar Gibbon
characters.description: A species of arboreal ape that went extinct in China. Today, it is only found in Southeast Asia.

characters.name: Oriental Pied Hornbill
characters.description: A small species of hornbill native to the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia.

characters.name: North American Scimitar Cat
characters.description: A species ofHomotheriumfound in North America. Like the Eurasian species, it is adapted to life in frigid landscapes, preferring the open grasslands of the mammoth steppe. Colossus Climb: How they hunt the much larger mammoths. David vs. Goliath: One member of the pack attacks an adult bull woolly mammoth head-on (literally), due to the pack being desperate, as the herds of smaller grazing animals have become scarce due to climate change. Though the first attack is unsuccessful, the pack trails the injured mammoth and their second attack is successful. Death from Above: Their second, successful attack on the mammoth starts when one of the cats leaps on top of him from a rock outcropping. Lightning Bruiser: Described as having the power of a lion and the agility of a leopard.

characters.name: Steller's Sea Cow
characters.description: A gigantic relative of the dugong that was once found across the North Pacific. These gentle creatures feed entirely on kelp, their sheer size, thick fat, and tough hides rendering them immune to both the frigid waters of their home and nearly all potential predators. Of all the extinct animals featured in the season, it was the most recent to disappear, having been exterminated by human hunters in the late 18th century; more specifically, around 1768, the same year that Captain James Cook began his voyages on the HMSEndeavour. Artistic Licence – Biology: They're shown to be capable of fully submerging, while in reality the animal was too buoyant to do that, unlike other sirenians (This made it all the easier for 18th century sailors to hunt them into extinction within just three decades). Gentle Giant: Sirenians have this reputation in general andHydrodamaliswere the biggest, growing as large as the biggest killer whale, while also being quite docile (as confirmed by historic reports). Kevlard: Their massive blubber and inch-thick skin renders them functionally impervious to the bear's attack. Nigh-Invulnerability: Its hide is so thick that not even a giant short-faced bear can tear through it. This saves a beached sea cow from becoming the bear's meal, despite otherwise being completely immobile on land until the tide rises again.

characters.name: North American Short-Faced Bear
characters.description: A giant tremarctine bear native to North America, ranging from Alaska to Mexico. This massive and powerful beast is the largest land carnivore to be found on the continent during the Ice Age. Bears Are Bad News: To most animals, a short-faced bear would definitely be a major threat; to the Steller's sea cow, it's only an annoyance. Dire Beast: LikeArctotherium, it's closely related to the little spectacled bear but is even larger than a polar bear. In terms of colorations, it resembles the blonde morph of the grizzly bear, another omnivorous North American ursid that coexisted with and outlivedArctodus. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: To polar bears, being a giant, light-furred bear that combs beaches and struggles at biting through the tough hide of a fatty marine mammal until the latter escapes back into the ocean (a sea cow instead of a walrus in this case). Though its colorations are more akin to a blonde grizzly bear (since the short-faced bear was ecologically far more comparable to a grizzly). Genius Bruiser: Subtly shown through his reaction to the unfamiliar sight of a beached sea cow, as he reacts with curiosity and wariness, first inspecting the beached giant and checking whether it's dangerous before trying (and failing) to eat it.Truth in Television, as bears are highly intelligent mammals on top of also being incredibly strong.

characters.name: North American Saber-toothed Cat
characters.description: The most iconic of all machairodont cats and the secondSmilodonspecies of the Ice Age, native North America and parts of South America. Cute Kitten: The cubs are very cute. Death of a Child: Narrowly averted, as a dire wolf grabs one of the cubs by the neck and nearly carries it off, when the mother finally frees herself and attacks. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: The cougar to the dire wolf's gray wolf. It not only utters cougar sounds (granted, so do the other machairodonts in the show), but it's likewise a solitary big cat that's physically more than a match for its pack-hunting canine rival. Help, I'm Stuck!: The mother's paw gets trapped in melting tar as the wolves approach.

characters.name: Dire Wolf
characters.description: A large wolf-like canine endemic to North America. It is a major competitor to the North American saber-toothed cat. Arch-Enemy: To the saber-toothed cats, as they were sympatric large predators that preyed on many of the same animals. Dire Beast: Averted, in spite of its name. It's around the same size as a North American gray wolf but stockier in build and with more powerful jaws. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: The gray wolf to the sabretooth's cougar. Far more obvious in this case, as they are large, pack-hunting canines with similar color schemes. Reused Character Design: It's briefly seen as a stand-in for a gray wolf in the first episode in the Eurasian cave setting.

characters.name: Elephant Bird
characters.description: An enormous ratite bird found on the island of Madagascar. It is both the largest bird known to science and the producer of the largest eggs known to science. This gigantic avian vanished much more recently than other extinct animals featured in the show, its youngest remains dating to the Middle Ages. Diurnal Nocturnal Animal: Studies show it was nocturnal like it's closest living relative the kiwi, yet they are only seen active during day time. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: The black plumage of the adults and the father's protective nature brings to mind a cassowary. Papa Wolf: A large male saves his chick from getting eaten by a giant fossa.

characters.name: Giant Fossa
characters.description: A larger, black-furred relative of the extant fossa. It is the largest terrestrial carnivore found on the island of Madagascar, making it a serious threat to most of the island's smaller animals. Like the elephant bird, this animal became extinct much more recently than most other Ice Age giants, being last recorded from the Middle Ages. Dire Beast: Relatively speaking. It's twice the size of the extant fossa but that only makes it as big as a large bobcat. Ironically, the elephant birds and some of the lemurs it coexisted with are prime examples of island gigantism. More broadly speaking, it and its extant relative are this to their mongoose cousins. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: It displays melanism like a leopard and is likewise an agile, arboreal feliform predator with a long tail. Mix-and-Match Critter: As a fossa, it's essentially a mongoose trying to be a cat, and this extinct species is comparable in size to a mid-sized felid. Our Cryptids Are More Mysterious: Its black coloration is likely based on reports of sightings of larger, darker-colored fossa than the modern fossa. The giant fossa became extinct so recently that even today, the Malagasy people make a distinction between thefosa mainty(black fossa) and the still-extantfosa mena(red fossa).

characters.name: Surfbird
characters.description: A small shorebird related to sandpipers and knots, native to the Pacific coast of the Americas.

characters.name: Caspian Tern
characters.description: The largest species of tern, found around large lakes and coastlines across the globe.

characters.name: Arctic Hare
characters.description: A species of hare adapted for frigid environments. Today, the species only lives in Greenland and the extreme north of Canada, but it was more widespread during the Ice Age.

characters.name: Great Horned Owl
characters.description: A large species of owl native to the Americas.

characters.name: Mule Deer
characters.description: A species of deer found in western North America.

characters.name: Lesser Hedgehog Tenrec
characters.description: A small tenrec species that resembles a hedgehog, endemic to Madagascar. Identical Stranger: You'd be forgiven for mistaking it for a hedgehog, yet it's more closely related to elephants and sea cows (all being afrotheres) than it is to actual hedgehogs, who in turn are closer to bats, carnivorans, ungulates and even us primates than to tenrecs (being boroeutherians).

characters.name: Madagascar Cuckooshrike
characters.description: A cuckooshrike endemic to Madagascar and some surrounding islands.

characters.name: Red Ruffed Lemur
characters.description: A species of lemur, which like all lemurs is from Madagascar.

characters.name: Chameleon
characters.description: A very distinctive kind of lizard. While they are found across Africa and Asia (plus one species in Europe), they are most abundant in Madagascar.

characters.name: Indri
characters.description: The largest living species of lemur, noted for its mournful cry.

characters.name: Vanga
characters.description: A type of passerine native to Madagascar, with a number of related species also being known from Asia and mainland Africa. They are an extremely diverse group, with many members having convergently evolved with other kinds of birds elsewhere in the world.

characters.name: Eurasian Jay
characters.description: A corvid native to Eurasia and Northern Africa.

characters.name: Human
characters.description: A species of intelligent, bipedal ape. Originating from Africa, these strange creatures have been spreading across the globe throughout the Ice Age, and they will one day come to rule the planet. Dawn of an Era: Their arrival is ominously presented as one, as they spread across the planet and establish dominance. Hero of Another Story: They only appear at the very end, but their globe-trotting adventures and eventual domination of the planet are alluded to.
